beats.text: Eight tasks. Some must wait for others. How long will the whole project take?
Draw the network, the PERT chart. Each circle is a task, with its duration in weeks.
Forward pass. Each task's earliest completion time, T E, is the T E before it, plus its own duration. Where two paths meet, take the larger.
Task one: five. Task three: eleven. Task four waits for both two and three, so thirteen. Keep going, and task eight finishes at twenty-two.
Backward pass. Start at the end with twenty-two, and walk back. Each task's latest completion time, T L, is the next task's T L minus the next task's duration. Where paths split, take the smaller.
Slack time is T L minus T E: how long a task can slip without delaying the project.
Task two has two weeks of slack. Task five has two and a half. Every other task has zero.
Zero-slack tasks are critical. The critical path is one, three, four, six, seven, eight. It is the longest path, and it sets the duration: twenty-two weeks.
Around it sit other tools. The work breakdown structure splits the project into tasks of at most forty hours. The Gantt chart shows the tasks as bars on a calendar.
